title: Fix the capability-pinning wait, and the two gates that hide it
description:
Three separate measured defects in dependency order, written 2026-10-03 at
merged `714cc0c` (PR #8), tree clean.

Source plan: `~/.opencode/plan/house-fix.md`

| # | Defect | Blast radius | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `house_pipe_wait` spins in `wfe` inside an `unsafe` FFI call and pins its capability | `blk init` / `virtio init` hang; any colocation with a must-progress thread | diagnosed, not fixed |
| B | `scripts/qemu-virtio-blk.exp` requires a QEMU machine property absent on Ubuntu 24.04's `qemu-system-arm` | every virtio gate fails on CI in 14 ms | diagnosed, not fixed |
| C | `nightly.yml` is one sequential job; the first red gate aborts all later steps | most of the gate suite has never executed in CI | diagnosed, not fixed |

Defect A blocks Phase 4 steps 9-11. B and C are why it was never caught in CI.

A and B are independent and can be fixed in either order. C is a workflow-shape
change and should land last, once there is a green suite to split.

Plan section 8 states the intended split: one `bug` for A1, one for A2, one
`chore` for the gate work in sections 2-3, and one for the related latent defect
in section 1.6.
## Success criteria

- [ ] `house-irq-dispatch-check` new; red before the fix, green after
- [ ] `house-virtio-blk-check` green, and no longer passing vacuously (drive attached, non-zero capacity asserted)
- [ ] `house-virtio-transport-check` green (shares `virtioInit`)
- [ ] `house-driver-check`, `house-ipc-check` green
- [ ] `house-fork-check`, `house-preempt-check` green (the `parkLoop` `c_pipeWait` site)
- [ ] `house-spin-hotplug-check`, `smp-check`, `SMP_N=4 smp-check` green
- [ ] `house-yield-spin-check` green, and re-checked that it is green for the intended reason
- [ ] `rust-check` + `rust/c-abi.md` audit green
- [ ] `haskell-check` 327 host checks, 0 fail
- [ ] Per-change gate `make check` (hvf + tcg) green

Not run and therefore not claimed: `smp-check-8` (4 GiB), `vm-check`,
`house-dynamic-root-check` (QEMU 11+, local only).

## After this epic

Phase 4 steps 9-11 unblock once defect A is green. `docs/TOOLCHAIN.md` currently
claims virtio-blk reaches the device through an endpoint; that stays false until
Phase 4 step 10 lands.

title: house_pipe_wait pins its capability: spin in wfe inside unsafe FFI
description:
Defect A1. Diagnosed in full, not fixed.

## The mechanism

`c_pipeWait` is `foreign import ccall unsafe "house_pipe_wait"`
(`kernel/H/Interrupts.hs:64`, used at `kernel/Kernel/Userspace/Process.hs:106`).
Its body (`rust/crates/house-libc/src/threads/threads.rs:1771`) is a `wfe` spin
bounded only by `house_uptime_ns()`. No foreign-call boundary, no Haskell safe
point, for up to 5 ms per call — and the dispatcher calls it in a loop,
forever. GHC cannot preempt inside an `unsafe` foreign call, so the capability
is pinned for the whole wait. `forkIO` puts the child on the parent's local run
queue, so dispatcher and shell land on the same capability; the shell then never
gets scheduled again and never prints `ok capacity=`.

## The asymmetry that is the whole bug

`poll` (`threads.rs:1683`) already has the guard `house_pipe_wait` lacks
(`threads.rs:1712-1720`, inside `poll()`):

```rust
let has_runnable = { lock; !RUN_HEAD[core].is_null(); unlock };
if has_runnable {
    house_sched_yield();      // give the runnable thread the capability
} else {
    /* wfe spin loop with deadline */
}
```

`poll` and `house_pipe_wait` have opposite caller populations, and only the
former has the guard. `poll`'s only caller is the EL0 syscall path
(`rust/crates/house-hal-aarch64/src/svc.rs:143`) — house-libc pthreads the house
scheduler owns outright, so `RUN_HEAD[core]` is authoritative for them.
`house_pipe_wait` has **no Haskell caller of `poll` anywhere in the tree** and
is instead called from GHC RTS threads, which reach it through a different
path. Those callers get no release point at all.

That also explains the two sites that work today: `parkLoop`
(`Process.hs:1310`) calls the same `c_pipeWait` and `house-fork-check` /
`house-preempt-check` pass, because the parked thread's supervisor is not
colocated with it on a capability. The dispatcher wedges because it is forked
*by the shell thread it then starves*.

## Premise to verify as part of the fix

The guard only helps if GHC's capability threads are house-libc `HouseThread`s,
so a runnable shell thread on the same capability appears in `RUN_HEAD[core]`.
GHC's threaded RTS creates its capabilities through the platform's
`pthread_create`, and house-libc implements that, so this is plausible — but it
is a premise, not a fact, and it is the difference between the fix working and
not. **Measure it.**

If the new gate goes green 10/10 the premise held and the diagnosis is confirmed
end to end. If it stays red, the premise is false — stop, and take a fallback.
Do not iterate on variations of this guard without re-checking the premise first;
if the shell's threads are not in `RUN_HEAD`, no amount of tweaking that flag
helps.

## Fix

In `rust/crates/house-libc/src/threads/threads.rs`, give `house_pipe_wait` the
same `has_runnable` -> `house_sched_yield()` pre-check `poll` has at line 1712.
Smallest change that matches existing style in the same file.

`house_sched_yield` (`threads.rs:565`) masks interrupts, spins on the scheduler
lock, reschedules the current *HouseThread*, and returns.

## Second at-risk call site, fixed by the same change

`Kernel/Userspace/Process.hs:1310`:

```haskell
_ <- liftIO (c_parkPipeFd >>= \fd -> c_pipeWait fd 5000)
```

Same function, same import, same defect, currently latent only because of where
the thread sits. Fixing `house_pipe_wait` in Rust fixes both. Fixing it in
Haskell per-import would not guarantee anyone remembers the second site.

## Fallback, if the premise fails

In order of preference:

- **6a.** Have `house_pipe_wait` park through the house-libc scheduler
  (`house_sched_block`, which already does `wfe` and re-checks the run queue)
  instead of its own spin loop.
- **6b.** Make `house_pipe_wait` return a bounded slice and let the *Haskell*
  caller loop, so the spin never spans more than one scheduler slice. This
  reintroduces polling and needs the poll budget measured, not guessed.
- **6c.** Fix the fork placement: start the dispatcher at boot rather than
  lazily inside `installHandler`, so it never shares a capability with a
  command handler. This treats the symptom and should be the last resort.

Whichever is chosen, record in the commit message why the `poll`-guard shape was
insufficient.

## Regression net

Confirm still green: `house-fork-check`, `house-preempt-check`,
`house-spin-hotplug-check`, `smp-check`, `smp-check-8`. `parkLoop`'s
`c_pipeWait` is covered by `house-fork-check`; if it is not, say so rather than
assuming.

Not run and therefore not claimed: `smp-check-8` (4 GiB, expensive),
`vm-check`, `house-dynamic-root-check` (needs QEMU 11+, local only).

`rust-check` plus a `rust/c-abi.md` audit: `threads.rs` changes, but
`house_pipe_wait`'s signature is unchanged, so the exported-symbol map must
still match.
## Steps to Reproduce

Every row is a full `make -C platform/aarch64 clean && make -C kernel clean && make house-build`, then QEMU under hvf with `-M virt,virtio-mmio-transports=8,gic-version=3` and a real `-drive` attached so the gate is not vacuous.

The isolation driver matches each command's **output** pattern (`ok device_id`, `ok capacity`), never the prompt, because the line editor redraws the prompt during echo and a prompt match reports 0 ms for everything.

| # | Change | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A0 | merged `714cc0c`, unmodified | **HANG** |
| B0 | `installHandler` does not fork the dispatcher | OK 23 ms |
| C0 | fork a thread whose body is only `C.yield` — no FFI, no locks | **HANG** |
| D0 | real `dispatcherLoop` + `C.yield` on **both** branches | **HANG** |
| E0 | fork a heartbeat thread: `c_uart_puts` then `C.yield` | OK 240 ms |
| F0 | real `dispatcherLoop`, `c_pipeWait` -> `C.yield` | **OK** |

Rates at A0: `virtio init 7` HANG 8/8. `blk init 7` HANG 8/10 — the two passes are the runs where the dispatcher fork won the race, not a second bug. `blk status 7` (171 ms) and `virtio scan` (190 ms) always pass, so the fault is in transport init, not `blkProbeCapacity`.

`blk init`'s own `serveEndpoint` fork was ruled out: stubbing it out changed nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `house-irq-dispatch-check` is **red** on the current tree (three iterations, not one)
- [ ] `house_pipe_wait` carries the same `has_runnable` -> `house_sched_yield()` pre-check `poll` has at `threads.rs:1712`
- [ ] Premise verified as part of the fix: gate green 10/10 confirms it; still-red means the premise is false and the fallback applies
- [ ] `house-virtio-blk-check`, `house-virtio-transport-check`, `house-driver-check`, `house-ipc-check` green
- [ ] `house-fork-check`, `house-preempt-check`, `house-spin-hotplug-check`, `smp-check`, `SMP_N=4 smp-check` still green (the `parkLoop` second call site)
- [ ] `rust-check` + `rust/c-abi.md` audit: exported-symbol map still matches (`house_pipe_wait`'s signature is unchanged)
- [ ] `haskell-check` 327 host checks, 0 fail
- [ ] Not claimed unless run: `smp-check-8` (4 GiB), `vm-check`, `house-dynamic-root-check` (QEMU 11+, local only)
close_reason: Fixed in 7e8ec98: the IRQ dispatcher's wait branch uses threadDelay 20000 instead of the blocking c_pipeWait FFI spin. The bead's poll-guard shape was rejected on evidence (RUN_HEAD holds house-libc pthreads; GHC green threads never enter it, so at -N1 there is nothing to yield to). Gate green 3/3 then 10/10; bounding the slice instead measured red 3/3. The two parkLoop c_pipeWait sites stay latent.

title: Add house-irq-dispatch-check gate (red before the fix, green after)
description:
Step 2 of the plan, and it must land **before** the fix so the fix has something
to turn green.

A dedicated gate, not `house-virtio-blk-check`: `virtio init 7` is 8/8 on the
buggy tree, so three consecutive successes is a reliable red.

## What to build

- `scripts/qemu-irq-dispatch-check.exp` — boot, run `virtio init 7` three times,
  assert an `ok device_id` within the bound each time, then assert the shell
  still answers `virtio status` afterwards (so a wedged-but-quiet machine cannot
  pass by timing out identically).
- `Makefile`: add `house-irq-dispatch-check` next to `house-virtio-blk-check`
  (line 239), add it to the `check` aggregate (line 495ff) and to `check-tcg`
  (line 473ff).

`scripts/gate-coverage.sh` fails if a new gate is not wired into `check` /
`check-tcg` / `nightly.yml`, so wire all of them in the same commit.

## Acceptance Criteria
 red on the current tree

Expect `virtio init` to hang on the first iteration.

## Why three iterations

`blk init` was 8/10, not 10/10. Any single-shot gate built on it is unreliable —
hence three iterations.

## Harness traps to not repeat

Two Expect harness bugs cost real time here:

1. In Tcl, `-re {"> "}` searches for the literal `"> "` because braces suppress
   substitution, so it matches nothing and every command looks like a hang.
2. A corrected `-re "> "` still matches the line editor's prompt redraw during
   echo, reporting 0 ms for everything.

Match each command's **output** pattern instead (`ok device_id`, `ok capacity`) —
the echo can never contain it.
close_reason: gate committed, red 3/3 hvf and 1/1 tcg on the current tree

title: Characterise A2: does Control.Concurrent.yield return the capability?
description:
Step 1 of the plan. **Do not skip this step.**

A2 is a defect *distinct* from A1 and is currently unexplained. It must be
characterised before it is fixed, because its blast radius is wider than the
dispatcher: the merged YIELD backoff in `Kernel/Userspace/Process.hs` and
anything else relying on `yield` to hand over the capability are equally suspect.

## What was measured

| # | Change | Result |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | fork a thread whose body is only `C.yield` — no FFI, no locks | **HANG** |
| E0 | fork a heartbeat thread: `c_uart_puts` then `C.yield` | OK 240 ms |
| F0 | real `dispatcherLoop`, `c_pipeWait` -> `C.yield` | **OK** |

C0 and E0 together say the dispatcher's *work* is irrelevant. A thread that does
nothing but `yield` still wedges; the same loop with one `c_uart_puts` added
does not. That falsified the working hypothesis at the time — "a missing
`C.yield`".

**A2 — `Control.Concurrent.yield` is not returning the capability.**
`H/Concurrency.hs:62` is `yield = liftIO IO.yield`, i.e. stock
`Control.Concurrent.yield`. If that actually yielded, C0 could not wedge.

Note the trap: adding `C.yield` around the `c_pipeWait` call is **not** a fix —
D0 proved that, and it is obvious in hindsight: the spin is *inside* the FFI
call.

## The characterisation

One build, three shell-visible counts, printed by a temporary `virtio`-less
shell path or read via `dmesg`:

1. a thread that loops `C.yield` forever, counting iterations;
2. a thread that loops `c_uart_puts` + `C.yield`, counting iterations;
3. a thread that loops `threadDelay 1` forever, counting iterations.

**If (1) counts far fewer iterations than (3) while both threads stay alive,
`yield` is not returning the capability and A2 is confirmed as a distinct
defect.**

**If (1) matches (3)**, C0 wedged for a different reason and this step has told
us nothing — in that case go straight to fixing A1 and treat A2 as open.

Cheaper alternative if the shell plumbing is awkward: `strings` the image for the
count format strings and read the counters off the UART trace. Same information,
no new command surface.

## Why this must precede the fix

The A2 fix differs depending on the answer, and guessing produces a fix that
passes the dispatcher gate and leaves the underlying scheduler bug live.

## If A2 cannot be answered cheaply

Fix A1 (which is fully diagnosed and sufficient to unblock) and file A2
separately rather than blocking on it.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Three counters exist and are readable (shell-visible output, or read off the UART trace via `strings` on the image for the count format strings)
- [ ] The `C.yield` count vs the `threadDelay 1` count is recorded as a measured number, not a description
- [ ] The verdict is recorded explicitly: either "A2 confirmed as a distinct defect" or "C0 wedged for another reason; A2 stays open"
- [ ] If confirmed, `house-yield-spin-check` is re-baselined before the A2 fix, so the fix has a before/after

title: Fix A2: yield does not return the capability
description:
Step 4 of the plan. **Only do this if the characterisation step confirmed
A2.**

## Fix, ranked by preference

- **4a.** Replace `H.Concurrency.yield`'s body with an explicit release point
  that is known to work in this RTS, and re-run the whole suite — A2's blast
  radius is every `yield` in the kernel.
- **4b.** If `yield` is fine and C0 wedged for a rate reason, drop this step and
  record that.

## The prohibition

**Do not paper over A2 by inserting an FFI call into hot loops to create
boundaries.** That is what made E0 pass; it converts a scheduler bug into a
per-site landmine.

## Blast radius to re-verify

A2's blast radius is every `yield` in the kernel. The merged YIELD backoff in
`Kernel/Userspace/Process.hs` (bounded-backoff arm past a threshold of 64
consecutive resumes) is equally suspect.

`house-yield-spin-check` must stay green, and must be re-checked that it is
green **for the intended reason** — that gate runs at `-smp 1` deliberately,
because at `-smp 2` both the fixed and unfixed arms are fast and the difference
is unobservable.

## Related evidence already in the tree

`docs/design/park-resume-capability-pinning.md` states that parking must
*return* from the unsafe `house_enter_el0` FFI so the RTS capability is released
while blocked. A bare `yield` was already measured insufficient (`4d4666e`:
"bare yield never freed it") — under the single-capability RTS a thread that is
immediately runnable again re-acquires the capability before a timer fires.
That is direct evidence that at least one `yield` site does not release.
## Steps to Reproduce

Inherit the C0/E0 measurement from the characterisation issue: fork a thread whose
body is only `C.yield` — no FFI, no locks — and observe the machine wedge, while
the same loop with one `c_uart_puts` added completes in ~240 ms.

Note that adding `C.yield` around the `c_pipeWait` call is **not** a fix — D0
proved that, and it is obvious in hindsight: the spin is *inside* the FFI call.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `H/Concurrency.hs:62` is either replaced with an explicit release point known to work in this RTS, or the issue is closed with 4b recorded
- [ ] The full suite is re-run — A2's blast radius is every `yield` in the kernel
- [ ] `house-yield-spin-check` stays green **and** is re-checked as green for the intended reason (the gate runs at `-smp 1` deliberately)
- [ ] No FFI call was inserted into a hot loop to manufacture a boundary

title: Virtio harness: probe for virtio-mmio-transports and stop passing vacuously
description:
Defect B, section 2 of the plan. Independent of defect A — fix in either order.

## Symptom

Nightly run `37136946248`, `slow-gates` job: fails in 14 ms with
`Property 'virt-8.2-machine.virtio-mmio-transports' not found` ->
`FAIL: eof before welcome`. Ubuntu 24.04 ships `qemu-system-arm` 8.2;
`virtio-mmio-transports` needs QEMU 10+.

This is the same QEMU-version requirement as `house-dynamic-root-check`, which
is already excluded from `check-tcg` **with a printed reason**.
`house-virtio-blk-check` was wired into nightly without the equivalent handling.

## Fix

- In `scripts/qemu-virtio-blk.exp`, probe for the property before building the
  `-M` argument string; fall back to plain `-M virt,gic-version=3` and print a
  single explicit line saying which property was dropped and why.
- Fall back to the 8-transport-less machine **and attach the device the old
  way**, so the gate stays non-vacuous. A skip that silently exercises nothing
  is worse than a failure.
- Add a `SKIP`-style banner the harness can grep, so the nightly log
  distinguishes "skipped, QEMU 8.2" from "passed".

## Second, independent problem in the same harness

With no `-device virtio-blk-device,drive=...` attached, every assertion takes
the `INFO` path and the gate **passes vacuously**. Add an explicit assertion
that the drive was attached and that the capacity probe returned a non-zero
sector count, so a misconfigured runner cannot report green.

The measurement harness used for section 1 attached a real 64 MiB image for
exactly this reason.

**Trap:** `house-virtio-blk-check` only fails when a drive is attached. Run
without `-device virtio-blk-device` it takes every `INFO` path and **passes** —
so a green run of `house-virtio-blk-check` proves nothing about the device
path. Any future "it's flaky, retry" instinct here is wrong; the pass is
vacuous.
close_reason: Guest widened to 32 virtio slots; all four virtio harnesses drop virtio-mmio-transports= and discover the device slot, so they run on QEMU 8.2 through 11+; qemu-virtio-blk.exp gained the missing non-vacuity guard. Also fixed two load-bearing 8-slot bounds the site enumeration missed: irq.rs house_irq_push ack range 48..56 -> 48..80 (slot>=8 livelocked in an IRQ storm) and Shell/Loop.hs handleConMirror's literal installConMirror 7 -> findConSlot. Verified hvf+tcg for driver/transport/net/con/irq-dispatch and hvf for blk; the blk tcg leg still hits a PRE-EXISTING slot-independent TCG livelock reproduced on pristine HEAD.

title: Split nightly.yml so one red gate does not abort the whole suite
description:
Defect C, section 3 of the plan. A workflow-shape change. **Should land
last**, once there is a green suite to split.

## Symptom

`nightly.yml` is a single job with sequential steps (`Filesystem and driver
gates`, `EL0 execution gates`, `SMP gates`, `Scaling gate`, `Memory matrix`,
`Miri`, `Slow SMP legs`). The first failure stops everything after it.

## Observed consequence

In run `37136946248` the virtio-blk failure meant these **never executed**:
`house-virtio-net-check`, `house-virtio-con-check`, the EL0 execution group,
the SMP group, `smp-check-8`, `vm-check`, `miri`, and the slow SMP legs.
`house-fs-check`, `house-ipc-check`, `house-driver-check` and
`house-virtio-transport-check` passed before it.

This is the root cause of the silence around defect A: **the gate that would
catch it has never been run.** Of the affected list, 5 were verified locally
during Phase 4 (`house-fs-check`, `house-ipc-check`, `house-driver-check`,
`house-virtio-transport-check`, `house-preempt-check`); the rest are unverified
anywhere. PR #8's green `gate` runs do not speak to it — `check.yml` runs
`make check-tcg`, which covers the Makefile's `check-tcg` legs only.

## Fix

Split into independent jobs on a matrix, or keep one job and give each gate group
`continue-on-error: true` plus a final `gate summary` step with `if: always()`
that fails the job if any group failed.

**The matrix is better**: it also parallelises, and each leg's result is visible
on its own.

## Also fix the schedule while here

`nightly.yml` was added 2026-09-30 and its cron is Sunday 03:00, so the first
window is 2026-10-05. The zero run count is the schedule, not a broken workflow.

GitHub disables scheduled workflows after ~60 days of repository inactivity, and
this repo's schedule has never produced a single run. Land this change together
with a `workflow_dispatch` run so the split is actually exercised before the
next cron.

## Consequence for the rest of the plan

Nothing in the capability-pinning work can be validated by CI until this lands,
and this cannot be validated until defect B lands. Expect to validate sections 1
and 2 of `house-fix.md` locally with `workflow_dispatch` afterwards.
notes: Update 2026-10-04 (house-1hc.5 landed): the QEMU-version blocker on this is GONE. house-virtio-blk/net/con-check and house-irq-dispatch-check no longer pass virtio-mmio-transports=, so all four run on Ubuntu noble's QEMU 8.2 as well as 11+, and all four were verified green locally on hvf and tcg. Moving them into check-tcg is therefore purely a gate-suite-shape decision now. NOT done in house-1hc.5 on purpose - it was out of scope there. Two things gate it: house-5wj (the blk tcg leg livelocks in an EL1 virtual timer storm, pre-existing) must be fixed before house-virtio-blk-check can be trusted on TCG; house-uqs (dynamic-root.img pin drift) is unrelated but currently red. house-driver-check and house-virtio-transport-check are also absent from check-tcg today despite working on QEMU 8.2 - they are already green on hvf+tcg with the 32-slot guest.

title: IRQ ring is not drained before the first installHandler
description:
Section 1.6 of `~/.opencode/plan/house-fix.md`. A real hole, currently latent.
**Separate issue — do not fold it into the capability-pinning fix.**

## The defect

From boot until the first `installHandler`, **nothing drains the IRQ ring**.
`house_irq_push` (`rust/crates/house-hal-aarch64/src/irq.rs:55`) drops the
record once the 256-entry ring is full. At a 100 Hz timer that is saturated in
under three seconds, so every IRQ between boot and first driver init is lost.

Nothing is currently broken by it — the timer has no `handlerTable` entry — but
it is a real hole and it is why "start the dispatcher at boot" keeps recurring
as an idea.

## Why it matters for the fallback choice

If the `poll`-guard fix for defect A1 does not hold its premise, fallback 6c is
"start the dispatcher at boot rather than lazily inside `installHandler`". That
fallback only actually fixes the ring-drop hole if the dispatcher is started at
boot — so the two are related, which is exactly why this must stay a separate
issue rather than being silently absorbed.

## Scope

Do not design the fix here beyond stating the hole. The fix depends on which
fallback path defect A1 takes.
## Steps to Reproduce

Boot and read `irqDrops` (or the `house_irq_push` drop counter) from `dmesg`
**before** the first `installHandler`, with a 100 Hz timer running and nothing
else consuming IRQs. At 100 Hz the 256-entry ring saturates in under three
seconds, so the counter must be sampled inside that window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The drop is observed and counted before the first `installHandler`
- [ ] A decision is recorded: drain the ring from boot, size it for the window, or document the loss as accepted with the bound stated
- [ ] `make check` green, and the boot-time IRQs before first driver init are accounted for

title: TCG virtio-blk gate livelocks in an EL1 virtual timer storm
description:
Pre-existing and slot-independent: NOT caused by the 32-slot widening.

## Symptom

The tcg leg of `scripts/qemu-virtio-blk.exp` livelocks after
`PASS: blk read <slot> 0`, before the next command (`write /a hello`) is even
echoed. QEMU sits at 97-99.8% CPU, expect is idle, and no further UART output
ever arrives. It is intermittent: one pristine run got as far as the
hostile-image mount stage before stalling in the burst loop.

## Measured signature

Reproduced with the harness plus `-monitor unix:/tmp/m.sock,server,nowait`
appended to the `--` args:

- `info registers` sampled repeatedly while it spins: the guest cycles
  through `house_uptime_ns_raw`, `house_timerfd_due`, `c_handle_irq` and
  house-libc internals. Under `-d int` the log is ~97k `Taking exception 5
  [IRQ]` lines; the dominant ELRs are inside `c_start_secondary` (the idle
  `wfe`), `is_aligned_to` and `house_sched_yield+0x394`.
- `RING_HEAD == RING_TAIL == 1` (read via the monitor `xp` on the .bss
  addresses from `nm`). Exactly ONE interrupt ever reached
  `house_irq_push`, so the storming interrupt is not a virtio slot SPI — it is
  an SGI or the EL1 virtual timer (INTID 27).
- `waitForCompletion` (`Blk/Server.hs`) is bounded at 200 x
  `threadDelay 2000`, so the blk used-ring poll is not what blocks.

## Proof it predates the 32-slot change

Reproduced identically on a stashed pristine HEAD tree, with the pristine
harness, at slot 7 (device parked there by `-M virt,virtio-mmio-transports=8`):
same stall point (`blk read 0 0 hello-blk`), QEMU at 99.6% CPU.

## Prime suspect

Two agents program the same counter. `threadDelay`/timerfd arms
`CNTV_TVAL_EL0` through `house_timerfd_*`, while `c_handle_irq`'s INTID 27
arm (`c_start.rs`) rearms it unconditionally from
`__c_house_timer_interval`. Each one undoing the other's deadline would give
exactly this: a bounded 400 ms wait that never expires because the timer is
re-armed underneath it.

## Why it matters

`house-virtio-blk-check` is in neither `check` nor `check-tcg`, so CI never

title: Step 15: scripts/house.exp prompt helper; convert 124 prompt waits
description:
Step 15, `~/.opencode/plan/house-phase4-loadbearing-shell-and-gates.md`.
Not blocked. This was also decided up front in Phase 4: build a shared Expect
helper library rather than patching harnesses one flake at a time.

## The bug it fixes, stated precisely

383 `expect {` blocks and **124 `-re "> "` prompt waits** across 32 harnesses,
all hand-written, all matching a prompt against a stream the kernel also writes
`dmesg` lines and EL1 kill logs to.

`03b1066` had to *delete* two prompt waits because the kill log garbled `> ` into
`>[kill]`. Deleting the assertion removed the hazard rather than the cause.

## Work

- [ ] New library with `house_prompt {label}`, `house_send {cmd}`,
      `house_expect {re label}`, each doing its own `catch {exec kill -9
      [exp_pid]}` and `eof` handling so no harness repeats that boilerplate.
- [ ] The helper matches the prompt as a **line-anchored** pattern and drains
      interleaved non-prompt output before waiting, so a stray dmesg line cannot
      eat the prompt.
- [ ] Convert in one mechanical commit, one harness per hunk, no behaviour change
      beyond the prompt matching. Do **not** convert harnesses opportunistically
      in the same commit as a behaviour change — that is what made `03b1066` /
      `6e0b314` hard to review.

## Acceptance Criteria

Run the full `nightly.yml` gate list locally before pushing; `make check` green.

## Risk

This touches 32 harnesses in one commit. It is mechanical, but it is 124 call
sites and a typo in the helper fails several gates at once. This is the one step
whose blast radius exceeds its conceptual size.

## Related Tcl trap

In Tcl, `-re {"> "}` searches for the literal `"> "` because braces suppress
substitution, so it matches nothing and every command looks like a hang. And a
corrected `-re "> "` still matches the line editor's prompt redraw during echo,
reporting 0 ms for everything. Match each command's **output** pattern instead —
the echo can never contain it.

title: A store to a plain RO page must yield EFAULT or a kill, never elr+4
description:
Step 18 of `house-phase2-correctness.md`; also review-and-plan step 26 / audit M5.

## The acceptance signal that is still unmet

The plan's wording: *"A store to an RO page delivers `EFAULT` or kills, **never
`elr + 4`**."*

`rust/crates/house-boot/src/c_start.rs:307` still returns `elr.wrapping_add(4)`.

## The path

`c_start.rs:260-308` — for `DFSC 0x0C..0x0F`, `WnR=1`,
`HOUSE_USER_VA_MIN..=HOUSE_USER_VA_MAX`, non-COW page — falls through to
`return elr.wrapping_add(4)`. So the store is **silently discarded and EL0 is
told it succeeded**.

## Why this needs a decision, not just a patch

The code carries a written rationale: read-back is observable, and parking would
livelock the loader's stub probe loop. So the two options are:

- park on a distinguishable request kind, or
- add the `vm-check` mprotect-RO read-back assertion the plan asked for

No later plan revisits it.

## Acceptance Criteria

silent success.

Note `vm-check` is an expensive memory/MMU matrix and **not** part of the
ordinary per-change gate.
## Steps to Reproduce

1. `mmap` a page in EL0, write to it.
2. `mprotect` it read-only.
3. Store to it again.

Observed today: the store is silently discarded and EL0 continues — the
`c_start.rs:307` fall-through returns `elr.wrapping_add(4)`. The plan's
acceptance signal is that this must deliver `EFAULT` or kill instead.

title: Retune the nine loader/linker caps as one reviewed decision
description:
## Epic context

The dynamic-linking umbrella's own status header names the open branch:
*"B (provenance (ii), GHC's libraries rebuilt against `house-libc`) is unstarted
with the cap retune it needs recorded as its own decision."*

This retune is the prerequisite for that whole branch, so it comes first.

## Why it is one issue and not nine

M1-M3.5, the loader-forgiveness slice (C1-C6, `d77be5a`), the phnum/segment
split with the `ByteString` representation, and **C8 (ABS64 + `DT_VERSYM`,
`011b538`) have all landed.**

retune, and that retune is still unauthorised: B1 fixed the representation so the
numbers would mean something … but no cap value moved."*

description:
Step 1 of `~/.opencode/plan/rust-stable-transition.md`. **[trivial]** This is the
actual bug fix and the unblocker; everything else is bookkeeping.

## The defect

`rust/Cargo.toml` line 9 declares `rust-version = "1.100.0"`, which is above the
latest stable (1.99.0). Cargo therefore hard-refuses to build the workspace on
*any* stable toolchain today.

Reproduced:

```
$ RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=stable cargo check
error: rustc 1.99.0 is not supported by the following package:
  p@0.1.0 requires rustc 1.100.0
```

The MSRV was set in `2a38214` ("chore(toolchain): pin rust-version 1.100.0
across workspace", 2026-09-06) while nightly was the only channel that could
satisfy it. It has been a forward-looking declaration ever since, and it is the
thing blocking stable.

Still true in the tree: `rust/Cargo.toml:9` reads `rust-version = "1.100.0"`.

## Fix

`rust-version = "1.100.0"` -> `"1.99.0"`.

All five crates inherit it via `rust-version.workspace = true`, so **no per-crate
edits**.

## Acceptance Criteria

`RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=stable cargo metadata --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml` no
longer errors on MSRV.

## Empirically verified

With MSRV lowered to 1.99.0, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` **compiles
clean on stable 1.99.0**. The only diagnostics are pre-existing `suspicious
definition of the runtime read/write/strlen symbol` warnings, which are
**identical on nightly** — confirmed by running the same clippy invocation on
nightly-2026-09-30. They are host-triple-only (hosted `cargo test` interposes std
symbols) and do not appear on the real gate, which is
`--target aarch64-unknown-none`. **Not a stable-transition regression; do not
"fix" it as part of this change.**

## Nothing else needs nightly

- Zero `#![feature(...)]` attributes in `rust/`.
- The only arch intrinsics in use are `core::arch::asm!` (stable since 1.59).
- No `global_asm!`, no `#[naked]`.
- `aarch64-unknown-none` std ships on stable (tier-2, present in the stable
  manifest's 116 `rust-std` targets). Only the *host* stable toolchain here
  lacks it installed — a local-install artifact, not a channel limitation.
- Everything is zero-dependency (`cargo deny` clean by construction), so no
  third-party MSRV bumps are implied.
## Steps to Reproduce

Verified still true in the current tree:

```
$ grep -n rust-version rust/Cargo.toml
9:rust-version = "1.100.0"
```

Against a scratch copy (project untouched):

```
$ RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=stable cargo clippy --workspace --target aarch64-apple-darwin -- -D warnings
error: rustc 1.99.0 is not supported by the following packages:
```

Upstream stable is 1.99.0 (2026-09-28, `b940084d7`). No 1.100/1.101 stable
channel exists.

title: Recalibrate mk-dynamic-probe.sh rustc/cargo pins for stable 1.99.0
description:
Step 5 of `~/.opencode/plan/rust-stable-transition.md`. **[trivial]** This is the
sharp edge of the whole transition.

## Risk, stated by the plan

Probe recalibration is the sharp edge. `mk-dynamic-probe.sh` asserts an exact
rustc commit *and* cargo version string. A stale value fails the TCG gate at
initrd build time, not at image build time — so it can pass `container-image`

title: dynamic-root.img pin does not match what mk-dynamic-root.py builds
description:
Pre-existing: NOT caused by the 32-slot virtio change.

## Symptom

`make dynamic-root-image` (and therefore `make check`, which runs it as a leg)
fails at the pin check:

```
sha256sum -c scripts/dynamic-root.sha256
sha256sum: WARNING: 1 computed checksum did NOT match
build/dynamic-root.img: FAILED
```

`scripts/dynamic-root.sha256` pins
`c6d2664ef0043eaa1261fcfb31c232ababc30ab3817b3051808c1edeb07fdb92`
but the build produces
`d52974ede39fddd7a0fe1d34a1a82d91a481c351207e8276f67d002c1a41a590`.

## Proof it predates the virtio change

Reproduced on a stashed pristine HEAD tree with the identical digest
(`d52974e...`), and `house-el0-tiny`, whose
`build/dynamic-probe/root/libc-missing.so.0` is the image's only input, has
no dependency on anything the virtio work touches.

## Two possibilities, not yet separated

1. **Genuine drift.** Something in the `house-el0-tiny` link output changed
   (toolchain, flags, or a genuine source change) and the pin was never
   regenerated. Then `scripts/dynamic-root.sha256` needs re-pinning — but
   re-pinning a hash you have not explained is how a real regression gets
   laundered, so find out which first.
2. **Non-determinism in `scripts/mk-dynamic-root.py`.** If the image embeds
   anything varying per run, the pin can never hold and every host fails
   differently. Cheap discriminator: build the image twice on a clean tree and
   compare the two digests. Equal => case 1; unequal => case 2.

## Also worth checking

`make check` has never run to completion — this leg has been the blocker, so
every leg after `house-dynamic-root-check` in that target is unproven locally.

## Related

`house-fiu` lists "`make house-dynamic-root-check` green locally" as an
unchecked phase criterion; this is the concrete reason it is not.

title: house-virtio-blk-check is red 5/5 at the house-1hc.1 defect: blk init forks the same capability-pinning dispatcher
description:
Found while landing house-1hc.2. That bead assumed `house-virtio-blk-check`
passes on the buggy tree; measured, it does not.

## Measured on 2026-10-03, commit 44537d6 (tree unchanged by house-1hc.2)

- `make house-virtio-blk-check` (hvf leg) — 4/4 red, `FAIL: blk init timeout`
- `make house-virtio-blk-check TCG_ONLY=1` (the leg `nightly.yml:51` runs) —
  red, `FAIL: blk init timeout`

`house-virtio-blk.exp` is byte-identical to HEAD and the diff touches nothing
on that path, so this redness is pre-existing, not a regression.

## Why the existing gate is wrong about itself

The `INFO` arms in that harness only cover a *missing device*:

```
-re "BlkBadSlot|BlkNotBlk|BadSlot|BadVersion" { puts "\nINFO: ..." }
```

A *hang* never produces those strings — it runs into the hard `timeout` arm at
line 60 and fails. So the "the INFO arms make every assertion optional, hence
it is 8/8 green" reasoning does not hold for this defect: the only way that
gate passes with a blk device attached is if `blk init 7` answers.

## Same defect, one layer up

`Blk.blkServerInit` (kernel/Kernel/Driver/Virtio/Blk/Server.hs:151) calls
`VTrans.virtioInit slot` when the slot is not already initialized. That is the
`Transport.virtioInit` which forks the transport IRQ dispatcher at
Transport.hs:176 — the dispatcher whose `house_pipe_wait` spin in `wfe` inside
unsafe FFI pins the RTS capability (house-1hc.1). `blk init` then forks a
second one for the request endpoint (Server.hs:165).

So `blk init 7` wedges for exactly the reason `virtio init 7` does.

## Why this needs its own bead rather than just a note on house-1hc.1

Two things house-1hc.1's fix should be checked against, and neither is
recorded anywhere today:

1. **house-1hc.1 turning green must turn this green too.** When A1 lands,
   `make house-virtio-blk-check` is the second, independent witness that the
   capability is no longer pinned — it exercises the blk request dispatcher
   (`blkRequestHandler`), which the new irq-dispatch gate never reaches.
2. **Until then the nightly is red.** `nightly.yml:51` runs this target, so
   the nightly has been reporting this failure as long as the defect has been
   present. If the nightly is currently green, that is itself worth asking
   about — the failure mode here is a hang, and a job killed by workflow
   timeout can look like an infra flake rather than a real red.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- After house-1hc.1 lands: `make house-virtio-blk-check` exits 0 on both legs.
- The nightly's `house-virtio-blk-check TCG_ONLY=1` leg reports red for the
  current tree, not green — confirmed rather than assumed.

Do **not** fix this by loosening `qemu-virtio-blk.exp`: making its `blk init`
arm optional again would hide the very failure this bead documents. The
overlapping work on the harness's vacuous-`INFO` design is house-1hc.5.
